newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP condemns French attacks on Spanish lorries.
newsitem.headline: EP condemns French attacks on Spanish lorries.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday condemned the repeated attacks by French farmers on lorries bringing Spanish farm produce into France and condemned Paris for not upholding Europe's single market laws.
"The European Parliament condemns unequivocally the recent and repeated attacks and the visible failure to take action by the French authorities," the EU assembly said in a resolution.

The unhindered attacks constituted "a serious threat to the free movement of goods, persons, services and capital within the European Union," the resolution continued, adding that free movement was crucial to the workings of the EU's internal market.

The non-binding resolution, which was tabled by Spanish Euro-deputies on behalf of five of parliament's eight political groups, demanded that the French government stick to its promise to pay compensation soon and that it take court action against the people involved.
Compensation should cover loss of markets as well as damage to vehicles and goods, the parliament said.

European Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro said the EU executive had brought infringement proceedings against France before the European Court of Justice and expected an Advocate-General to give an opinion on July 8.

Anne Christine Poisson, a French farming MP from the anti-federalist Europe of Nations party, told the assembly that while she deplored the attacks, the main problem lay with the flaws in the organisation of EU agricultural markets, which allowed the Spanish to dump their cheap strawberries and tomatoes on the French market.
